title: Google Home opens early MCP access to third-party AI agents
friendlyTitle: AI agents can start working with Google Home devices
summary: Google is opening early access to a Google Home MCP server that lets compatible agents work with connected devices and event history. Users can grant access for tasks such as controlling lights, checking camera summaries or building a home dashboard.
friendlySummary: Google is testing a connection that lets compatible AI agents control smart-home devices and read some home activity information after you approve access.
whyItMatters: This is a concrete step from conversational assistants toward agents acting in physical spaces. Anyone testing it should grant the narrowest permissions possible and treat camera history, locks and household routines as sensitive data.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This could make home automation easier. Give an agent only the permissions it needs, especially for cameras, locks and private household information.
